correctness.rationale: The algebraic GAL reduction and exact rational recurrence follow by identity. For any fixed positive initial density all iterates stay in the positive unit interval for sufficiently small detuning. Affine comparison yields uniform c(k+1)<=y_k<=C(k+1) through k=O(1/epsilon); summation of the drift gives y_k=2k+O(epsilon k^2+log(k+1)+1). Consequently R(y_k)=3/(2k)+O(epsilon+(1+log(k+1))/k^2). The geometric reweighting differs from 1 by O(epsilon k), so the weighted nonlinear remainder sums to (3/2)log n+O(1). Exact variation of constants then yields the two-sided expansion with uniform O(epsilon) error. Critical convergence follows from summable remainders. Standalone code verifies algebra and representative finite cases but is not the infinite proof.

It is common to recovery and extinction detunings with a specific nonzero 3/2 coefficient and remains valid uniformly at finite positive scaled times.
